findings.title: Remove stale backup test artifact
findings.description: The diff adds `packages/core/tests/services/CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E`, a stale duplicate of the real test file. It still calls the old one-argument `createContextPipeline` API at `packages/core/tests/services/CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E:29`, `:35`, `:59`, `:99`, `:119`, and `:141`, while `packages/core/src/services/CoreServiceFactory.ts:29-33` now requires `{ adoptionStateWrites }`. The `.ts-E` suffix is not matched by the Vitest include glob in `packages/core/vitest.config.ts:5`, `packages/core/tsconfig.json` only includes `src/**/*`, and `eslint.config.mjs:9` ignores `**/tests/**`, so this file is dead duplicated code that can drift or mislead maintainers. Delete it or merge any intended changes into the real test file.

findings.title: Avoid more positional plumbing at changed API boundaries
findings.description: `ContextIntegrator` now has seven positional constructor parameters; `packages/core/src/services/CoreServiceFactory.ts:44-52` passes all seven, and tests use `null, null, null` chains such as `packages/core/tests/services/ContextIntegrator.test.ts:384`. `generateContext` also grew to five positional parameters in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:58-63`, with call sites at `:202` and `:267`. The TypeScript rules require named parameters via object destructuring for functions with 3+ parameters. These signatures are fragile, hard to read, and make it easy for a JS caller to shift an overrides object into `adoptionStateWrites`; use a named options/dependency object instead.

findings.title: Adoption state is persisted before the build is known to succeed
findings.description: `createAdoptionResolver` writes `in_progress` at `packages/core/src/adoption/adoptionResolver.ts:129`, then returns facts for rendering. Context generation happens afterward, but `packages/core/src/services/ContextTemplateEngine.ts:47-66` catches generation failures and returns `ERROR: Context generation failed`, while `packages/core/src/services/ContextIntegrator.ts:119-125` returns `⚠️ Error generating context` for non-`AdoptionError` failures. Those paths do not rethrow, so a first Phase 0 build can mutate `.context-forge.toml` and still return an error prompt/exit normally. This conflicts with the project rule to fail explicitly. Gate the write on successful generation, or rethrow/roll back the state when generation fails.

findings.title: template_preview's read-only contract still permits guide-checkout writes
findings.description: `template_preview` is registered with `readOnlyHint: true` and a no-side-effects description, and the new call at `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:267` only passes `adoptionStateWrites: 'read-only'`. However `generateContext` still calls `ensureGuideForProject()` at `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:89-94`; that helper calls `GuideManager.ensureCheckout()` (`packages/core/src/guides/GuideManager.ts#ensureCheckout`), which explicitly initializes an uninitialized submodule checkout. Therefore a “read-only” preview can still mutate the guide checkout on fresh clone/submodule projects. Either make guide readiness read-only for `template_preview`, or update the annotation/description and tests to state this side effect.

findings.title: New tests leak a console.error spy across later tests
findings.description: The new adoption error-stub test at `packages/core/tests/services/ContextIntegrator.test.ts:433` calls `vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {})` but never restores it. The earlier permissiveness test at `packages/core/tests/services/ContextIntegrator.test.ts:354` has the same pattern, the file has no `afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())`, and `packages/core/vitest.config.ts:3-8` does not enable `restoreMocks`. Later tests in the same file run with `console.error` suppressed, hiding diagnostics and making test order matter, which violates the testing rule that tests run independently. Restore the spy in `finally`/`afterEach` or add a file-level cleanup.
